item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Sun Nov 1, 8:00 AM — Marin County Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Free Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market. Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine. www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.description:

We’ll make calls to get people to the polls on Election Day and share the exciting reasons to support candidates like Mary Peltola in Alaska for U.S. Senate, and Abdul El-Sayed (U.S. Sen.), William Lawrence (MI-07), and Christina Hines (MI-10) in Michigan! Sign up today to help make calls to support progressives across the countr
Source: Indivisible Sonoma County (Mobilize)

item.title: Día de los Muertos: Meet the Artists & Altaristas — Sun Nov 1, 2:00 PM — Museum of Sonoma County
item.description:
**Join us at the Museum of Sonoma County for a special opportunity to connect with the local artists and altaristas featured in our 30th Annual Día de los Muertos exhibition. Throughout the hour, participating artists and altaristas will share brief gallery talks about their work, creative processes, and the stories and traditions behind their offerings. Visitors are also invited to chat with the artists, ask questions, and learn more about the personal meaning and cultural significance of this annual exhibition.**
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Kids Upcycle Clothing and Accessories Event — Sat Nov 7, 12:00 PM — St. Paul's Episcopal Church parish hall
item.description:
The parents of children at St. Paul's Episcopal Church in Healdsburg are sponsoring an Upcycle Clothing Event at the church parish hall on Saturday, Nov. 7, from 12-4 p.m. Everyone is invited to come by the hall at 209 Matheson Street, grab a grocery-size bag, pay a fee of $20 and fill the bag with all the clothing, shoes, books, toys and other children's items it will hold. All of the items are gently-used and have been collected and sorted by the parents of the kids who attend St. Paul's. Most items are gently used but some are practically new and have simply been outgrown. A few particularly dressy items will be separately priced. Proceeds from the sale will be used to fund children's activities at the church, such as buying art supplies for the newly-refurbished Sunday School room. That room will be open during the sale for children to visit while their parents shop. Members of the Episcopal Church Women will assist with the sale.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Wine Country Marine Corps Birthday Ball — Sat Nov 7, 5:30 PM — Jacuzzi Family Vineyards
item.description:
Brigadier General Andrew T. Priddy, Commanding General of the 1st Marine Division, based at Camp Pendleton in Southern California, will be Guest of Honor at Wine Country Marines’ 2026 Marine Corps Birthday Ball. The November 7 event at Jacuzzi Family Vineyards will celebrate the Corps’ 251st birthday.
Sonoma Valley’s annual event began in 1985. A formal Marine Corps Birthday Ball is an unusual gathering for a community as small as Sonoma, and its setting in the heart of California Wine Country has helped it become known as a “Destination Ball,” drawing Marines from across the country.
The local event is part of the worldwide Marine Corps Birthday Ball tradition honoring the Corps’ founding on November 10, 1775. Marines gather around that date each year to celebrate their shared history and service.
